title: Invertibility of the derived unit from acyclic images of injectives
statement: Let $C,D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and chosen derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $L:C\to D$ and $R:D\to C$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive] with an adjunction $L\dashv R$, with $L$ exact and $R$ left exact. Suppose the adjunction unit $I\to RLI$ is invertible for every injective object $I$ of $C$, and $LI$ is $R$-acyclic for every such $I$, meaning $R^qR(LI)=0$ for all $q>0$. Then the unit of the bounded-below derived adjunction $D^+(L)\dashv R^+R$ is invertible at every $K\in D^+(C)$.

proof.text: Represent K by a bounded-below complex T of injective objects of C. Such a representative exists by enough injectives: replace a bounded-below complex representing K by an injective resolution. Naturality of the derived unit transports its invertibility across the resulting isomorphisms in D+(C).

On T the derived unit factors as the termwise unit T to R(L(T)), followed by the right-derived-functor comparison on L(T), up to the canonical exact-functor localization isomorphism. The first factor is an isomorphism termwise by the unit hypothesis, hence is an isomorphism in the homotopy and derived categories.

The bounded-below complex L(T) has R-acyclic terms by hypothesis. The acyclic-complex computation of the right derived functor makes its comparison to R+(L(T)) invertible; this is the existing theorem Functor.isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_of_rightAcyclic used in the source proof. Thus the second factor is invertible. The localization comparison is also an isomorphism, so cancellation gives invertibility of the derived unit on K.
